lead: Based on what you told me, your number one constraint is:
h1_soft: Nobody defaults to the cheapest option when one choice is clearly dominant.
h1: But when there’s no clear differentiation, [[price becomes the only thing left to compare.]] That’s a positioning problem.
fix_p: Find a category you can win. Pick a **less crowded category**, then own it and dominate it with your clear differentiator.
s1_kick: Find the least crowded category you can win
s1_h1: Every time you say you’re faster, cheaper or better, you’re inviting buyers to [[compare you]] with cheaper options and familiar names.
s1_body: So before you change a single word of your marketing, pick a category you can actually win. That doesn’t mean inventing a brand-new one, because then you’d spend years explaining what it is. It means finding a space buyers already understand, where far fewer businesses are competing.
m_was_call: The crowded category, where every agency and every alternative promises lead gen outcomes
m_now_call: The few agencies sitting where CRO, lifecycle email and positioning meet
s2_kick: Dominate it with the gap nobody has filled
s2_h1: Your Contrarian POV™ is the **gap only you can fill**.
s2_body: You don’t brainstorm it in a meeting. You find it in the one place where your customer, your market and your process all overlap.
b_cust: What they keep saying, what they’re struggling with, and what they want most.
b_mkt: What the alternatives are doing, and where they keep falling short.
b_proc: What you do differently that fills the gap the others leave behind.
win_s: of our sales calls now become clients. It worked so well that I’m now writing a book on it.
next1: So how do I find what makes me different?
iceberg: There are three more steps to this, but we’ll talk about those on our call.
quad: Picking a category you can win, then owning it with one clear difference, is quadrant 2 of the Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™ OS.
cta: Show me how to stop competing on price
up_next: Next question: What have you already tried to improve your revenue?
